title: HeraPay Dedicated Capacity Discovery
next_steps: Send dedicated capacity pricing and options
Share SOC2 and security pack link
Schedule on-prem deployment deep-dive with infra team
Run a 1-week benchmark with 4-GPU reserved pool
action_items: Morgan: send pricing and sizing options by 2026-09-30
Diego: provide benchmark template and sample config by 2026-10-02
Ravi: share current GPU utilization & latency SLOs by 2026-09-30
summary: Initial discovery for dedicated GPU capacity. Customer is evaluating reserved pools for inference with isolation needs and burst into hosted. Key concerns: latency SLOs, multitenancy isolation, KMS integration, SOC2 compliance, and predictable cost. Agreed to run a 1-week benchmark and share security docs and pricing.
topics: Dedicated capacity sizing, isolation and VPC/private deployment, burst strategy and autoscaling policy, security (SOC2/KMS/audit logs), benchmarking and next steps
transcript:
[00:00] Morgan Lee: hey everybody thanks for joining, uh we really appreciate you carving out time. i'm Morgan from Redwood, ae on the account. diego from our se team is here as well. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Sonia Patel: good thanks, Sonia here. busy week but excited to talk about dedicated.
[00:17] Ethan Brooks: hey, ethan here. quick background — we're running a mix of in-house inference and some hosted endpoints, looking for more predictable latency and costs.
[00:25] Diego Alvarez: great, thanks ethan. can you give us a sense of current qps and token distribution? like p99 targets and average seq len?
[00:34] Ethan Brooks: sure, so production is around 200 rps peak, 60 average, most prompts are short — 32 to 256 tokens occasionally longer for reconciliation flows. our p95 latency target is 250ms, p99 ideally under 600ms but we can tolerate some tails during batch jobs.
[00:50] Ravi Gupta: from infra, we care about data isolation. we can't have other tenants touching our models or KV caches. also need SSO + SAML, and KMS for key management.
[01:03] Morgan Lee: totally understood. those are common for payments. dedicated is designed for reserved GPU pools with tenant isolation. we can do VPC peering or private endpoint, bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via KMS integrations, and RBAC for access controls.
[01:15] Sonia Patel: good. are there differences between dedicated and private in terms of hardware control? we might want to tune quantization and models over time.
[01:23] Diego Alvarez: yes — dedicated gives you reserved GPUs in our managed cluster, you get dedicated capacity and isolation at the tenancy level, but the control plane is Redwood-managed. private (VPC/on-prem) hands you the control plane too — more ops burden but maximum control. for most customers who want predictable throughput without operating infra, Dedicated is sweet spot.
[01:43] Ethan Brooks: what's the burst story? we have large spikes during end-of-day processing that push QPS x3 for a few minutes.
[01:51] Morgan Lee: we support burst capacity options. typically customers keep a reserved baseline and configure burst pools that can consume unused capacity in the region or fall back to hosted nodes. burst incurs different pricing, and we can set policies to auto-burst or require manual approval.
[02:05] Ravi Gupta: so if we burst into hosted, does data go through shared hardware? is user data retained?
[02:10] Diego Alvarez: excellent question. when bursting to hosted, requests can go to logically segregated hosted instances; we have contractual controls for data retention and can avoid caching on shared KV where necessary. if regulatory constraints forbid any shared hardware, we'd recommend Private.
[02:28] Sonia Patel: we are regulated — PCI-like requirements. we need audit logs, immutable audit trails, and quarterly attestation. we also need encryption at rest inbound to our KMS.
[02:39] Morgan Lee: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and can integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping. we'll share our security pack after this call (link: https://redwood.ai/security-pack). audit logs and trace exports can be sent to your SIEM via S3 or syslog.
[02:55] Ethan Brooks: nice. can you explain how autoscaling works within a dedicated pool? we want to scale latency-sensitive paths quickly.
[03:03] Diego Alvarez: autoscaling is policy-driven. you can scale replicas by GPU count, or scale up model variants. there's fast-scaling for low-latency operations — warm pool pre-spawn, continuous batching tuned for short sequences, and KV cache warm-up. scale decisions use metrics and can be constrained by min/max reserved limits.
[03:22] Ravi Gupta: and what about preemption? if we reserve say 4xA10 GPUs, we need guarantees that no noisy neighbor affects us.
[03:30] Morgan Lee: reserved capacity means the GPUs are dedicated to your tenancy, so no preemption by other customers. noisy neighbor concerns are minimized; for extra isolation we can provision single-tenant racks.
[03:40] Sonia Patel: pricing — ballpark per month for a 4-GPU reserved pool?
[03:44] Morgan Lee: i'll send exact pricing in the follow-up. ballpark depends on GPU type and term length. for A100/A10-equivalent SKUs, monthly committed pricing with annual term is typically in the low tens of thousands; without committing it's higher. we also provide bursts at a premium. i'll add concrete numbers to the email.
[03:59] Ethan Brooks: okay. on the model side, we run a private finetuned LLM, 7B-ish, quantized int8. will that run on your runtime? any restrictions?
[04:10] Diego Alvarez: yes, we onboard custom models. runtime supports quantized weights, int8 and int4 profiles depending on the arch. some ops might need custom kernels; we collaborate on a quick onboarding pass. we can run a compatibility test during the POC.
[04:24] Ravi Gupta: do you support multi-tenant model hosting where we deploy multiple model versions in the same pool?
[04:29] Diego Alvarez: you can host multiple versions, with model pinning and rollout policies (canary, A/B). KV cache and prefix caching are tenant aware, but be mindful of memory for large key-value caches.
[04:40] Sonia Patel: what's the SLA for Dedicated? we need uptime and latency SLOs tied to penalties for enterprise deals.
[04:47] Morgan Lee: we offer SLA-backed uptime for Dedicated; latency SLOs are part of the enterprise contract and include rollback/fallback policies. governance and support tiers determine credits. we'll include SLA samples in the security pack.
[04:59] Ethan Brooks: great. can we talk about the benchmark you suggested? we want to reproduce p99 numbers with our workloads.
[05:06] Diego Alvarez: typical approach: we propose a 1-week benchmark where we provision a 4-GPU reserved pool, replay a synthetic but representative workload (your production traces scrubbed), measure p50/p95/p99, token/sec, and cost per 1M tokens. we provide a benchmark harness and sample configs.
[05:22] Ravi Gupta: and the harness runs in our VPC? what's network topology for traffic during benchmark?
[05:28] Morgan Lee: we can run the bench either through a private peered endpoint or you can run a local load generator that hits the pool's private endpoint. logs/statistics are exported to your S3.
[05:39] Sonia Patel: on encryption, we must approve key lifecycle. how does BYOK work in practice?
[05:44] Diego Alvarez: BYOK: you provide key material or key handle via supported KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, or customer HSM). we do envelope encryption; we never store raw key material. keys can be rotated by policy, and we provide key usage audit logs.
[05:58] Ethan Brooks: are there any limitations on model size or token length in Dedicated vs Hosted?
[06:04] Diego Alvarez: limits are mostly hardware-bound. Dedicated pools can be sized for larger context windows; compilation and kernel selection will be tuned per model. hosted variants may have stricter limits to keep instance density high. for your 7B model with 4k context it's fine.
[06:17] Ravi Gupta: what's the deployment time? if we sign a reserved contract today, how long to stand up capacity?
[06:22] Morgan Lee: typical lead time is 2-4 weeks for capacity provisioning and networking setup for Dedicated. Private on-prem can be longer depending on procurement.
[06:31] Sonia Patel: okay, timeline wise we want a pilot next month. procurement needs T&C and security pack.
[06:36] Morgan Lee: we'll get the security pack and a SOC2 report over after this. i'll also include a pricing matrix: 4-GPU baseline + burst options + on-demand rates.
[06:45] Ethan Brooks: one more — observability. we need per-route token-level costing and tracing to correlate latency regressions.
[06:52] Diego Alvarez: Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdowns, per-model dashboards, tracing hooks, and error analysis. you can export traces to Jaeger/Zipkin or our traces sink.
[07:03] Ravi Gupta: any gotchas re: KV cache warmup — we have cold-start issues when scaling up replicas.
[07:09] Diego Alvarez: known issue, we recommend warm pool pre-spawn and cache snapshotting to speed warm starts. we can help design a cache warm-up recipe for your flows.
[07:20] Sonia Patel: are there contractual constraints on data residency? some of our customers require EU-only.
[07:25] Morgan Lee: yes regional constraints are supported; we can restrict dedicated capacity to EU regions only and ensure data residency. for stricter contracts, Private deployments in selected regions are an option.
[07:36] Ethan Brooks: can you run through a quick security checklist we can give Procurement?
[07:40] Morgan Lee: sure: SOC2 Type II, SAML SSO, RBAC, KMS BYOK, audit logs export, VPC peering/private endpoints, encryption at rest and in transit, pen test summaries. we'll attach the checklist to the follow-up.
[07:56] Sonia Patel: awesome. i noticed earlier you mentioned model quantization recommendations. how prescriptive are those?
[08:02] Diego Alvarez: our Optimize team provides quantization and model recommendations per workload — e.g., int8 for good quality/cost tradeoffs, sometimes int4 for batch-only workloads. we also provide A/B evals on quality regressions.
[08:16] Ethan Brooks: sounds good. what success criteria should we set for the pilot?
[08:20] Morgan Lee: i'd suggest: reproduce p95/p99 latency targets under peak load, cost per million tokens below your threshold, successful KMS integration and audit log export, and no data residency violations.
[08:33] Ravi Gupta: who will be our main contacts during the pilot?
[08:36] Morgan Lee: i'll be your AE; Diego will run technical ops. we'll assign a CSM if we move to contracting.
[08:44] Sonia Patel: ok recap please?
[08:47] Morgan Lee: recap: we'll send pricing and sizing options, SOC2/security pack and checklist, benchmark harness and template, and a proposed 1-week pilot plan for a 4-GPU reserved pool with burst policies. next meeting to review pricing and schedule the bench.
[09:03] Ethan Brooks: and action items?
[09:06] Morgan Lee: action items — Morgan send pricing by 9/30, Diego share benchmark template by 10/02, Ravi share utilization traces by 9/30.
[09:16] Sonia Patel: perfect. thanks everyone.
[09:19] Diego Alvarez: thanks, we'll follow up with links.
[09:22] Morgan Lee: thanks, bye.
[09:24] [call ends]
